recipes.name: Country-Fried Steaks with Sweet Onion Gravy
ingredients_raw: 3 very large sweet onions (such as Vidalia®), thinly sliced

steps.text: Combine flour, cornstarch, onion powder, garlic powder, salt, black pepper, and cayenne pepper in a large shallow dish; set aside ⅓ cup in a small bowl. Gently press steaks in remaining flour mixture until well coated.
Melt 1 tablespoon butter with 1 tablespoon oil in a large skillet over medium heat. Add steaks; pan-fry until golden, about 4 minutes per side, flipping once. Transfer steaks to a platter.
Melt remaining 1 tablespoon butter with remaining 1 tablespoon oil in the skillet over medium heat. Add onion; cook and stir until translucent, 5 to 7 minutes.

Sprinkle reserved ⅓ cup flour mixture over onions; cook and stir about 1 minute. Stir in stock and milk; bring to a boil, stirring constantly, until gravy thickens, scraping the browned bits of food off the bottom of the skillet with a wooden spoon.
Return steaks to the skillet, submerging them in gravy. Cover the skillet, reduce heat to low, and simmer, stirring occasionally, until steaks are very tender, about 45 minutes.

raw_recipe.headline: Country-Fried Steaks with Sweet Onion Gravy
raw_recipe.description: This country-fried steak recipe dredges cube steaks in a spicy flour coating, pan-fries, then gently simmers in rich, sweet onion gravy until super tender.

review.reviewBody: This is just the way my grandmother and mom make it. I omit the cayenne pepper because my family doesn't like it spicy. I don't always remember to put in the cornstarch and it's great either way. Thanks!

Amazing and very easy to make. I substituted half of the milk with cream. And, I coated with the flour mixture, then dredged in beaten egg, and coated with the flour mixture again before frying. I will absolutely be making this again.

This is a great recipe. I use 1-2 onions and put a beef bouillon cube in the gravy. Instead of simmering on top of the stove, put meat and gravy in a covered pan in the oven for 45 minutes at 350 degrees. If I don't have beef stock on hand, use a packet of Au Jus Mix. Keep the flour/spices in a ziplock bag it's handy. I did use cayenne pepper. Thanks for sharing!

Easy, but somewhat bland. I seasoned the meat, dredged in plain flour, and added flour & cornstarch to the onions. Maybe only add 1 T of cornstarch, as the gravy was very thick. Also, add a browning agent (Gravy Master).

This is a good recipe. I made a few changes to it but not much. First of all, I adjusted the recipe for 6 serving and used 6 top blade steaks (that I pounded out). Then I seasoned the meat on both sides with a little garlic powder, onion powder, cayenne and salt before dredging in the flour mixture. I didn't have sweet onions, so I used 3 large yellow onions instead. Because I adjusted the servings I reserved a 1/2 cup of flour mixture instead of 1/3 cup. Followed the recipe as stated from the flouring to the return of the steaks to the gravy. Because the meat was almost done, I only simmered in the gravy for about 20 minutes. The gravy was a little bland so I added a few extra shakes of salt to it. Turned out great! I will definitely make this again. Thanks for the recipe!

I made this for my husband and I, and we both loved it! The sweet onion gravy was delicious! The only change that I made was to lightly beat 2 eggs, and in breading the cube steaks, dredged in the flour mixture, then the eggs, then the flour mixture again. My coating did not come off of my cube steaks after simmering in the gravy, as one of the other reviews stated. Could be because of the change I made in coating my steaks, or just the fact that you really need to dredge the steaks and get the flour into your steaks. I will definitely use this recipe again as my go-to country fried steak recipe!
Used left over prime rib...poked with a meat tenderizer used egg milk wash and left out cayenne. I also used a deep fryer. The gravy I used 1% milk and a little whipping cream, OMG Delicious gravy.
Very good. Added a few shakes of Worcestershire, dab of A-1 sauce, ounce of red wine. McCormick steak seasoning in place of salt. Also sure to have lots of onions and make lots of gravy.
I used half gluten free flour and half almond flour. Steaks came out great! Quite tasty gravy.

Absolutely delicious! Didn't have onion powder though. Also doubled the cayenne but it didn't make it spicy. I love spicy so next time I'll triple or quadruple it. :) Didn't have milk. Used heavy whipping cream. Also, I only cooked the meat on each side for about two minutes instead of four. Came out very tender. Oh and I actually used venison because it's what I had on hand. Would recomend to anyone!

This was a very tasty recipe!! I changed only a couple of things. I only used one extremely large onion vs. three. I added a jar of mushrooms and a few red pepper flakes. I also added just a dash of kitchen bouquet for flavor. Otherwise, the meat was as tender as could be and gravy was delicious!! Try it, you will love it!!

Easy to make and full of flavor. I double the amount of cayenne to kick up the spice level. Cubed steaks are fork tender. My family loves this dish served with creamed potatoes, green peas and cole slaw. We have this excellent dish 6 to 8 times per year.
Gravy is so good. Followed exactly.
Loved it! I cook only when we forget to buy frozen microwave dinners. My grown children thank me for not cooking. They loved this!!!
This was as delicious as everyone says. The Vidalia onion give a tinge of sweet to a savory dish.

I have made this twice with venison cube steak. Really a very good way to cook venison. If this is this good with venison, you who use beef will be really delighted. As normal, prep time is more than the recipe calls for. It takes me an hour and 45 minutes to do this well.
Next time I make this I will beat out the meat so it won't burn so much. Otherwise it was delicious. Oh and I also added Johnny's Garlic seasoning.
My hubby and I loved this, so it's a keeper. It was my first time making a gravy and it was a hit. :D
